concept.name: Post-trade review
concept.definition: The structured analysis of completed trades - thesis versus execution, rule adherence, and outcome in R-multiples - conducted after the trade to extract lessons and feed them back into the playbook. Sound review evaluates decisions by ex-ante quality, not merely by whether the trade made money.
concept.intuition: The trade is not over when you exit; it is over when you have written down what the market just taught you.
concept.mechanics: Each closed trade is logged with screenshots, entry and exit rationale, and rule-adherence scoring; patterns across trades (which setups, times of day, or error types drive results) are aggregated in daily and weekly reviews. Review explicitly separates process grades from outcomes to avoid outcome bias.
concept.failure_modes: Review fails when small samples are over-interpreted, when only losers are reviewed, or when hindsight bias rewrites the original rationale. Reviews without recorded pre-trade reasoning degrade into storytelling.
concept.misconceptions: Reviewing only P&L is not review; the unit of analysis is the decision. Nor is review an occasion for self-punishment - its function is system improvement, not emotional accounting.
concept.example: A trader tags all trades by setup in her journal and finds that 80% of losses come from afternoon counter-trend trades, which she then removes from her plan.

citations.source: Mike Bellafiore, One Good Trade: Inside the Highly Competitive World of Proprietary Trading (Wiley, 2010) - publisher page
